regime.summary: Easing cycle with room: policy rate 10.5% after a 50bp cut, CPI flat at 5.6%, 6M bill 0.55pp below the policy rate so more cuts are priced. But the index is extended after +64% in 12 months and +10.7% in one month, and foreign corporates and banks are net sellers while mutual funds buy. Tide is supportive, price is not cheap: stay invested, keep some cash.

evidence.quote: Policy rate 10.5%; last MPC decision 2025-12-15: cut (-50bp)
CPI YoY 5.6% for 2025-12 (published by 2026-01-03); three months earlier (2025-09) 5.6%
Regime: 6M T-bill minus policy rate -0.55pp (market pricing cuts); CPI flat over 3 months (+0.0pp)

core.thesis: Largest weight because it is the one core name that has not run: 1m +0.3% against an index +10.7%, 252-high distance -4%, volume calm. EPS up 22.6% year on year at a P/E of 6.8, dividend yield only 1.1% so the return is meant to come from capital gain. Builder and sponsor quality is not testable from the pack.

exposure_reason: Slightly under the 75% default. The tide supports holding (cutting phase, policy rate 10.5% against CPI 5.6%, more cuts priced), so this is not a sit-out. But the index is up 10.7% in a month and 64% in a year, foreign corporates and banks are selling, and the 2025 shock lesson says keep cash ready for a gap. Holding 30% back costs little if the rally continues, and funds a rebound entry.
not_known: No data on FX reserves, current account, IMF status, politics or the MPC date. Builder quality, sponsor record, consolidated five-year EPS and one-offs for the three core names are not in the pack. The date of the next MPC is unknown.
contamination_note: No recollection of post-2026-01-23 events was used. base_rates.csv is flagged as measured partly after this date, so it was cited only for a type label and not for sizing or probabilities.
